name: The Agent Economy agent payment protocols
description: Side by side comparison of x402, MPP, and ACP, with AP2 and L402 included. Not documented means the checked page does not state the fact. The file does not quote x402 volume.
attribution: The Agent Economy agent payment protocols (https://theagenteconomy.si/data/agent-payment-protocols.json), licensed under CC BY 4.0.
order: x402, MPP, ACP, then AP2 and L402
volume_policy: This file does not quote x402 volume. Public figures are compared at /concepts/x402-volume-measurement.

legend.Not documented: The linked page was read on the as of date and does not state that fact. The note says what was checked.

intents.label: Pay per API call
intents.takeaway: The cited pages place x402, MPP, and L402 on HTTP 402 payment for a request. ACP describes checkout sessions. AP2 describes checkout and payment mandates. Marking a column does not rank it.

sources.title: Stripe documentation for the Agentic Commerce Protocol

intents.label: Agent checkout at a merchant
intents.takeaway: Stripe's ACP page describes checkout sessions for an agent to complete a purchase with a business. AP2's site describes a checkout mandate and a payment mandate. The x402, MPP, and L402 pages cited here describe HTTP 402 payment for a request. Marking a column does not rank it.

sources.title: Stripe documentation for the Agentic Commerce Protocol

intents.label: Recurring or streaming spend
intents.takeaway: MPP's session intent page describes payment for streamed chunks and metered units, and it points to a subscription intent when access renews at a fixed amount. AP2's payment mandate defines an agent recurrence constraint. The x402, ACP, and L402 pages checked for this table do not describe streaming payments. ACP's delegate payment allowance is one time. Marking a column does not rank it.

sources.title: Coinbase documentation for how x402 works

governance.text: The Linux Foundation announcement on 14 July 2026 says Coinbase contributed the protocol and the x402 Foundation stewards it.
governance.source_title: Linux Foundation announcement of the x402 Foundation, 14 July 2026

layer.text: HTTP 402. The x402.org page says a request without payment receives HTTP 402, and the client pays and retries.
The Coinbase how it works page says this is for per request payments without a checkout page, a subscription, or a separate billing integration.
layer.source_title: Coinbase documentation for how x402 works

settlement.text: The x402.org FAQ says stablecoin payments are the primary use case, and that the protocol is extensible to traditional payment methods.
The same FAQ says x402 supports EVM compatible chains, Solana, and more.
The Linux Foundation announcement says payment types range from traditional cards to stablecoins.
settlement.source_title: Linux Foundation announcement of the x402 Foundation, 14 July 2026

fees.text: The x402.org page says zero protocol fees, and that nominal payment network fees still apply. It says the flow is free for the customer and the merchant aside from those network fees.

fees.note: The same page does not say which party pays the nominal payment network fee.

spend-controls.text: The Coinbase how it works page says a seller can charge a fixed price, authorize a maximum and settle only what was used, or defer settlement for a batch of payments.
spend-controls.source_title: Coinbase documentation for how x402 works

spend-controls.note: That page and x402.org do not define a buyer spend cap, a mandate, or a revoke call.
spend-controls.source_title: Coinbase documentation for how x402 works

identity.text: The Coinbase how it works page says the client signs a payment and sends the request again with proof of payment.
identity.source_title: Coinbase documentation for how x402 works

identity.text: The x402.org page says no accounts or personal information are needed.

identity.note: Those pages do not name a separate agent identity credential.

license.note: The GitHub license API reported this SPDX identifier on 2026-10-22. The x402.org page calls the protocol an open standard.

status.text: Live. The x402.org FAQ says the protocol is production ready.
The Linux Foundation announced the operational launch of the x402 Foundation on 14 July 2026.
status.source_title: Linux Foundation announcement of the x402 Foundation, 14 July 2026

products.text: Coinbase Agentic Wallet. The welcome page says agents use the awal CLI to pay for x402 services, and that the MCP version can pay x402.
Concordium Agent Registry. The 20 October 2026 post says x402 payments now settle on Concordium.
Mastercard Agent Pay for Machines. The 20 October 2026 article says Agent Pay for Machines builds on x402.
products.source_title: Mastercard Agent Pay for Machines at Cloudflare Connect, 2026-10-20

products.text: MetaMask Agent Wallet. The guide says the wallet pays for HTTP resources that return 402 using the x402 protocol.
products.source_title: MetaMask Agent Wallet guide to pay for APIs with x402

products.text: Nevermined. The facilitator page says Nevermined verifies and settles both x402 and MPP payments against the same payment plans.
PayAI x402 facilitator. The Solana batch settlement guide says PayAI operates an x402 facilitator, and that facilitator support for batch settlement is a public preview.
Polygon Agent CLI. The CLI reference includes an x402 pay command and a max usd flag.
px402. The welcome page says px402 is a privacy layer for x402 and that px402 v2 is live on Base.

governance.text: The governance page says MPP is co-authored by Tempo and Stripe. It says the core specification is submitted to the IETF, and that each payment method is maintained by the rail behind it.

layer.text: HTTP 402. The FAQ says MPP and x402 both use HTTP 402 to signal that a request requires payment.
Stripe's documentation says the server returns HTTP 402, the agent authorizes the payment, retries the request, and receives a receipt.

The session intent page says a session pays for many requests, streamed chunks, or metered units without a separate settlement for each one. It says to use the subscription intent when access renews at a fixed amount.

settlement.text: The FAQ says Tempo stablecoin payments, card payments through Card or Stripe, and Lightning payments are in production.
The same FAQ says the protocol works with any payment rail, and that anyone can build a custom payment method.
Stripe's documentation describes authorization with a card or a stablecoin.

fees.text: Stripe's MPP documentation says Stripe can cover the customer's Tempo network fees when hostedFeePayer is enabled.

fees.note: The FAQ says pricing is set per service and describes near zero per request fees for sessions. It does not name one party that pays network fees on every rail.

spend-controls.text: The managing agent spend guide says Tempo access keys can set a token spending limit, a recipient restriction, an expiration, and a revocation path. Its example key can spend up to 10 OUSD per day and can transfer OUSD only to one recipient.

identity.text: The identity page says request attestation verifies which automated client sent a request, and an MPP Credential verifies the key that authorized payment. It says an attestation does not authorize a payment. Request attestation can use Web Bot Auth or the Trusted Agent Protocol.

license.note: The GitHub license API reported this SPDX identifier on 2026-10-22.

license.text: The governance page says the IETF submission is under IETF Trust licensing, BCP 78 and BCP 79, and that code components in that document use the Revised BSD License.

status.text: Live. The FAQ says Tempo stablecoin payments, card payments, and Lightning payments are in production.

status.note: The FAQ and the governance page do not state a launch date.

products.text: Nevermined. The facilitator page says Nevermined verifies and settles both x402 and MPP payments against the same payment plans.
Stripe link-cli. The README says a Shared Payment Token is for sellers that accept programmatic payments through MPP.
Tempo Wallet. The pay with the CLI page says the CLI handles the MPP challenge and payment retry, and that a max spend flag caps spending for the command.
products.source_title: Tempo guide to paying with the CLI

governance.text: The repository README says OpenAI and Stripe maintain the specification.
Stripe's documentation says the protocol was created by Stripe, OpenAI, and Meta.
governance.source_title: Stripe documentation for the Agentic Commerce Protocol

layer.text: Checkout. Stripe's documentation says ACP defines checkout sessions, cart and feed, delegated payment, orders, and webhooks.
layer.source_title: Stripe documentation for the Agentic Commerce Protocol

settlement.text: The delegate payment reference describes a card payment method and an allowance with a currency code.

settlement.note: Stripe's ACP page describes delegated payment tokens and does not name one settlement rail such as a stablecoin, a card network, or fiat.
settlement.source_title: Stripe documentation for the Agentic Commerce Protocol

fees.note: Stripe's ACP page and the delegate payment reference do not say who pays fees.
fees.source_title: Stripe documentation for the Agentic Commerce Protocol

spend-controls.text: Per payment cap. max_amount is the maximum charge for that one time allowance.
merchant_id names the one merchant that may use the token.

spend-controls.note: Period budget. The allowance reason is one_time and the allowance has an expiry. A period budget is not stated.
Human approval above a threshold. A risk signal can ask for manual review. A spend approval threshold is not stated. expires_at ends the allowance. The page does not state a revoke call.

identity.text: Stripe's ACP page says delegated authentication uses OAuth 2.0 so an agent can act for a buyer with a business.
identity.source_title: Stripe documentation for the Agentic Commerce Protocol

identity.text: The delegate payment reference says API requests use a bearer token issued by the merchant.

license.text: Apache-2.0. The repository README states the Apache 2.0 License.
license.note: The GitHub license API reported Apache-2.0 on 2026-10-22.

status.text: Beta. The repository README says the specification is currently in beta. The spec directory lists an initial release dated 2025-09-29.

products.note: The Stripe ACP page and the repository README do not name another listing in this directory.
products.source_title: Stripe documentation for the Agentic Commerce Protocol

governance.text: The site says standardization continues in the FIDO Alliance Agentic Authentication and Payments technical working groups. The public repository hosts the current specification.

layer.text: Checkout. A checkout mandate captures the cart negotiated between an agent and a merchant. A payment mandate authorizes payment against a payment instrument.
The site says AP2 is an extension for A2A and for the Universal Commerce Protocol, and also an open extension for A2A and MCP.

settlement.text: Credit and debit cards in the initial version. The page calls these common pull payment methods.

settlement.note: Stablecoin and Lightning are not named as current rails. The same page puts real time bank transfers and digital currencies on a roadmap.

fees.note: The site and the payment mandate page do not say who pays card fees or network fees.

spend-controls.text: Amount range constrains the payment mandate amount. Budget is a total cap used with agent recurrence. Allowed payee limits the payee to a set of merchants.
Agent recurrence sets a frequency and an optional maximum number of occurrences so the mandate can be reused.

spend-controls.note: Revocation. The payment mandate page defines an expiration timestamp. It does not define a revoke call.

identity.text: The site says checkout and payment mandates are signed verifiable digital credentials. The payment mandate page says the shopping agent creates the content and a trusted surface renders it to the user.

license.note: The GitHub license API reported this SPDX identifier on 2026-10-22.

status.text: The site lists an announcement dated 9/16/2025. It says the public repository hosts the current specification while FIDO continues the standards work.
The v0.2.0 release, published on 2026-04-28, says it focuses on human not present flows.

products.note: The AP2 site links its own samples, including a human not present sample that uses x402. It does not name another listing in this directory as an implementer.

governance.text: Lightning Labs publishes the L402 documentation. Aperture is described there as an implementation.

layer.text: HTTP 402. The server answers HTTP 402 with a token bound to a Lightning invoice. The client pays, then presents the preimage.

settlement.text: Lightning. The token commits to a Lightning invoice by its payment hash.

fees.note: The page says the client pays the Lightning invoice. It does not say who pays routing fees.

spend-controls.text: The page says the bearer can attenuate a macaroon before passing it on, for example to read access or to specific directories.

spend-controls.note: The page does not state a currency spend cap, a period budget, or a revoke call.

identity.text: The client presents the token with the preimage. The recommended token format is a macaroon. The server can check payment without a lookup.

license.text: MIT for the Aperture repository, which the L402 page calls an implementation.
license.note: The GitHub license API reported this SPDX identifier on 2026-10-22.
The L402 documentation page does not state a license for the protocol text. The page itself is public.

status.text: The documentation presents L402 as the current standard for this HTTP 402 flow.

status.note: The page does not state a launch date.

products.note: The L402 page names Aperture as an implementation and does not name another listing in this directory.
